To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1. A color distractor presented at fixation captures attention independent of its feature certainty; 2. This effect is stable over time; 3. This effect is present in all three blocks;

attention capture by a distractor in the color dimension is present even if feature uncertainty is not present and that attention capture by distractors defined in the same dimension as the target does not depend on feature uncertainty.
a color distracter presented in the same dimension (color) as the target captures bottom-up attention independent of feature certainty.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how visual search is affected by the presence of an irrelevant distractor.
the question of why irrelevant distractor objects are not always ignored in visual search.
the question of how the visual system deals with irrelevant information that can be defined in the same feature dimension as the target.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the influence of down-weighting of irrelevant features on attention capture is a matter of the feature dimension, but not the feature certainty.
the influence of distractor uncertainty is not a matter only of feature uncertainty, but also of feature dimension.
feature uncertainty is not a necessary condition to produce bottom-up attentional capture.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
feature uncertainty is only one of many factors that determine whether or not an irrelevant singleton distractor will capture attention.

the effect of down-weighting of irrelevant single color channels within the feature map used for search is dependent on whether these channels are shared with the target (in this case: no effect) or not (effect).
feature uncertainty only matters when distractors and targets are in different feature dimensions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
feature uncertainty can be a matter of the feature dimensions, but it is not a matter whether a feature is defined in the same dimension or not.
feature uncertainty is not a necessary condition for the occurrence of bottom-up attention capture.
attention capture by an unexpected distractor in a visual search task can be brought about by a variety of mechanisms.
